steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on CopulaCPTS, a copula-based conformal prediction method for multi-step time series forecasting: motivate calibrated uncertainty and confidence regions, introduce conformal prediction, describe the multi-step forecasting setting and the gap in existing methods, and list our contributions.

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Calibrated uncertainty; confidence regions
  - DL used widely in high-risk settings (healthcare, transportation)
  - model should produce calibrated uncertainty reflecting own confidence
  - confidence regions = common approach to quantify prediction uncertainty
  - validity: A (1-\alpha) -confidence region \Gamma^{1-\alpha} for a random variable y is valid if it contains y ’s true value with high probability: {\mathbb{P}}[y\in\Gamma^{1-\alpha}]\geq 1-\alpha.
  - infinitely large region trivially valid; want minimal area while valid = efficiency
- Conformal prediction (CP)
  - confidence regions with finite-sample validity guarantees
  - no assumptions on prediction model or data distribution
  - generality, simplicity, guarantees -> popular: time series prediction, drug discovery, safe robotics
- Setting
  - multi-step forecasting from a set of independent sequences
  - example: vehicle trajectory prediction (Figure 1): predict k future steps from past t steps
  - trajectories independent of each other; time steps within a trajectory temporally dependent
- Gap
  - same challenges: EEG forecasting (patients independent), short-term weather forecasting (local meteorology history independent)
  - multiple steps ahead -> want "cone of uncertainty" over the entire forecast
  - existing CP for time series: coverage only for individual time steps, or regions too inefficient (long horizons, multivariate)
- CopulaCPTS
  - practical + effective CP algorithm for multi-step forecasting
  - Copula-based Conformal Prediction for multi-step Time Series
  - copula = multivariate CDF modelling dependence between random variables
  - joint uncertainty over future steps -> shrink regions, keep validity
  - copulas used for CP before, but multiple-target prediction, non-temporal, no validity proof
- Contributions
  - general UQ algorithm for any multivariate multi-step forecaster
  - proof: valid regions for full horizon
  - sharper + more calibrated than SOTA baselines on two synthetic + two real-world datasets

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Deep learning models are now widely used in high-risk settings, for example healthcare and transportation. In these settings it is important for a model to produce calibrated uncertainty that reflects how confident it is. A common approach to quantify prediction uncertainty is confidence regions. A (1-\alpha) -confidence region \Gamma^{1-\alpha} for a random variable y is valid if it contains y ’s true value with high probability: {\mathbb{P}}[y\in\Gamma^{1-\alpha}]\geq 1-\alpha. Note that we could make the confidence region infinitely large to make it valid. But to have a useful confidence region we also want its area to be as small as possible while it stays valid; this is called the efficiency of the region.

Conformal prediction (CP) is a powerful framework that produces confidence regions with finite-sample guarantees of validity. It also does not make assumptions about the underlying prediction model or the distribution of the data. Because CP is general, simple, and has statistical guarantees, it has become popular for many real-world applications, including time series prediction, drug discovery and safe robotics.

In this paper we look at the setting of multi-step time series forecasting from a set of independent sequences. Take the problem of vehicle trajectory prediction, shown in Figure 1. We have a dataset of trajectories, and the task is to predict the future trajectory for k steps given its past trajectory of t time steps. We assume that the trajectories are independent of each other, but within each trajectory the time steps are temporally dependent.

- Gap
  - same challenges: EEG forecasting (patients independent), short-term weather forecasting (local meteorology history independent)
  - multiple steps ahead -> want "cone of uncertainty" over the entire forecast
  - existing CP for time series: coverage only for individual time steps, or regions too inefficient (long horizons, multivariate)
- CopulaCPTS
  - practical + effective CP algorithm for multi-step forecasting
  - Copula-based Conformal Prediction for multi-step Time Series
  - copula = multivariate CDF modelling dependence between random variables
  - joint uncertainty over future steps -> shrink regions, keep validity
  - copulas used for CP before, but multiple-target prediction, non-temporal, no validity proof
- Contributions
  - general UQ algorithm for any multivariate multi-step forecaster
  - proof: valid regions for full horizon
  - sharper + more calibrated than SOTA baselines on two synthetic + two real-world datasets
  - extension to forecasts of varying lengths

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Deep learning models are now widely used in high-risk settings, for example healthcare and transportation. In these settings it is important for a model to produce calibrated uncertainty that reflects how confident it is. A common approach to quantify prediction uncertainty is confidence regions. A (1-\alpha) -confidence region \Gamma^{1-\alpha} for a random variable y is valid if it contains y ’s true value with high probability: {\mathbb{P}}[y\in\Gamma^{1-\alpha}]\geq 1-\alpha. Note that we could make the confidence region infinitely large to make it valid. But to have a useful confidence region we also want its area to be as small as possible while it stays valid; this is called the efficiency of the region.

Conformal prediction (CP) is a powerful framework that produces confidence regions with finite-sample guarantees of validity. It also does not make assumptions about the underlying prediction model or the distribution of the data. Because CP is general, simple, and has statistical guarantees, it has become popular for many real-world applications, including time series prediction, drug discovery and safe robotics.

In this paper we look at the setting of multi-step time series forecasting from a set of independent sequences. Take the problem of vehicle trajectory prediction, shown in Figure 1. We have a dataset of trajectories, and the task is to predict the future trajectory for k steps given its past trajectory of t time steps. We assume that the trajectories are independent of each other, but within each trajectory the time steps are temporally dependent.

Many real-world tasks have the same challenges as this example, like EEG forecasting (each patient is independent) and short-term weather forecasting (the local meteorology history is independent), etc. These tasks need predictions for multiple time steps into the future, so we want a "cone of uncertainty" that covers the whole course of the forecasts. The existing CP methods for time series data either only give a coverage guarantee for individual time steps, or they produce confidence regions that are often too inefficient to be useful, especially for long horizons or in multivariate settings.

In this paper, we present a practical and effective conformal prediction algorithm for multi-step time series forecasting. We introduce CopulaCPTS, which is a Copula-based Conformal Prediction algorithm for multi-step Time Series forecasting. A copula is a multivariate cumulative distribution function that models the dependence between several random variables. We use copulas to model the uncertainty jointly over the future time steps, and in this way we can make the confidence regions much smaller while keeping them valid. Copulas have been used for conformal prediction before, but that work focuses on multiple target prediction in non-temporal settings and does not give a validity proof.

In summary, our contributions are:

- We introduce CopulaCPTS, a general algorithm for uncertainty quantification that can be applied to any multivariate multi-step forecaster.

- We prove that the confidence regions produced by CopulaCPTS are valid for the full forecast horizon.

- CopulaCPTS gives much sharper and better calibrated uncertainty estimates than state-of-the-art baselines on two synthetic and two real-world benchmark datasets.

- We extend CopulaCPTS to get valid confidence intervals for time series forecasts with varying lengths.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Deep learning models are becoming widely used in high-risk settings such as healthcare and transportation. In these settings, it is important that a model produces calibrated uncertainty that reflects its own confidence. Confidence regions are a common approach to quantify prediction uncertainty [1]. A (1-\alpha) -confidence region \Gamma^{1-\alpha} for a random variable y is valid if it contains y ’s true value with high probability: {\mathbb{P}}[y\in\Gamma^{1-\alpha}]\geq 1-\alpha. Note that one can make the confidence region infinitely large to satisfy validity. But for the confidence region to be useful, we also want to minimize its area while keeping it valid; this is known as the efficiency of the region.

Conformal prediction (CP) is a powerful framework for producing confidence regions with finite-sample guarantees of validity [2,3]. Furthermore, it makes no assumptions about the underlying prediction model or the data distribution. Its generality, simplicity, and statistical guarantees have made CP popular for many real-world applications including time series prediction [4], drug discovery [5] and safe robotics [6].

This paper considers the setting of multi-step time series forecasting from a set of independent sequences. Consider the problem of vehicle trajectory prediction, illustrated in Figure 1. Given a dataset of trajectories, the task is to predict a future trajectory for k steps given its past trajectory of t time steps. We assume that the trajectories are independent from each other, while within each trajectory the time steps are temporally dependent.

Many real-world tasks present the same challenges as this example, such as EEG forecasting (each patient is independent), short-term weather forecasting (local meteorology history is independent), etc. They require predicting multiple time steps into the future, so it is desirable to have a "cone of uncertainty" that covers the entire course of the forecasts. Existing CP methods for time series data either only provide a coverage guarantee for individual time steps [7,4] or produce confidence regions that are often too inefficient to be useful, especially in long horizons or multivariate settings [8].

In this paper, we present a practical and effective conformal prediction algorithm for multi-step time series forecasting. We introduce CopulaCPTS, a Copula-based Conformal Prediction algorithm for multi-step Time Series forecasting. A copula is a multivariate cumulative distribution function that models the dependence between multiple random variables. By using copulas to model the uncertainty jointly over future time steps, we can shrink the confidence regions significantly while maintaining validity. Copulas have been used for conformal prediction [9], but that work focuses on multiple target prediction in non-temporal settings and does not provide a validity proof.

In summary, our contributions are:

- We introduce CopulaCPTS, a general uncertainty quantification algorithm that can be applied to any multivariate multi-step forecaster.

- We prove that CopulaCPTS produces valid confidence regions for the full forecast horizon.

- CopulaCPTS produces significantly sharper and more calibrated uncertainty estimates than state-of-the-art baselines on two synthetic and two real-world benchmark datasets.

- We extend CopulaCPTS to obtain valid confidence intervals for time series forecasts of varying lengths.
